scenes.text: An AI can finish your sentence. Can it change what you're able to notice afterward?
scenes.query: laptop with an AI chat interface generating a reply on its screen, stable desk framing

scenes.text: A stranger intelligence test than another question we already know how to grade.
scenes.query: pencil marking answers on an exam paper on a desk

scenes.text: Learning. Reasoning. Handling the unfamiliar. Useful clues to intelligence; there isn't one universally accepted definition.
scenes.query: hands fitting a piece into a jigsaw puzzle

scenes.text: Picture two workshops. Same tools, same unfinished chair. You arrive with shaky hands.
scenes.query: wide view of a carpenter working in a wood workshop with timber and a workbench

scenes.text: In the first, a machine builds it while you watch. Perfect joints. You're impressed.
scenes.query: CNC wood carving machine cutting a wooden workpiece in a workshop

scenes.text: In the second, it helps you discover why wood splits against the grain.
scenes.query: close-up of a chisel moving through wood grain and lifting small shavings

scenes.text: Both produce a chair. One also changes what you can do tomorrow.
scenes.query: a carpenter working on a wooden chair in a workshop

scenes.text: Here's my proposed second test: what does an intelligence make possible beyond itself?
scenes.query: a young seedling growing in soil in a time lapse

scenes.text: One mathematics study found that unrestricted AI help improved students' practice performance.
scenes.query: student writing mathematical equations in a notebook

scenes.text: After access ended, those students performed worse independently than students who'd practiced without it.
scenes.query: student writing answers on an exam paper independently

scenes.text: A tutor designed to safeguard learning largely avoided that loss. Design changed the outcome.
scenes.query: student using a laptop beside a mathematics notebook at a desk

scenes.text: A better chair doesn't automatically mean a more capable carpenter.
scenes.query: carpenter measuring a wood plank with a ruler

scenes.text: Sometimes you just need the chair. Your washing machine can keep its lecture on personal growth.
scenes.query: colorful clothes spinning inside a washing machine drum

scenes.text: But when understanding matters, the hidden question changes: did the task improve, or did your grip?
scenes.query: carpenter gripping a chisel and carefully carving wood at a workbench

scenes.text: Maybe intelligence has a footprint beyond the system displaying it. A capacity left in someone else.
scenes.query: footprints left in sand as a person walks away

scenes.text: A sharper question. A mistake you can finally recognize. A method you can carry away.
scenes.query: a pencil eraser removing a mistaken mark from paper

scenes.text: That's an effect worth measuring. It doesn't establish consciousness or replace tests of the machine's abilities.
scenes.query: close-up of an electronic circuit board and processor in changing practical light

scenes.text: And help can remain available. Instructions, tools, other people: your workshop has always contained more than you.
scenes.query: two carpenters working together over a plan at a workbench

scenes.text: Can you inspect the joint, question the plan, and choose what you're building?
scenes.query: carpenter inspecting a wooden joint and checking its fit
